body:
## Overview

This PR introduces `skills/work-designer` as a general work-design assistant for reasoning about goals, requirements, architecture, contracts and design decisions. **Review** is its first work-design mode, producing an evidence-backed integration report without implementing fixes. **Revise** maintains the skill following the work-planner authoring pattern. These are its only modes.

## Changes

### Review Procedure

- **Coverage follows the project's design and implementation.**
  The procedure reads architecture and design documents, traces requirements through declarations and consumers, and derives checks from each affected branch's languages, constructs, schemas and responsibilities.
- **Findings identify the result actually reviewed.**
  The report records heads, targets, merge bases, tested combinations and proposed merge or deployment order. Revision freshness and CI checkout evidence determine whether observations still apply.
- **Missing evidence remains visible.**
  Executed checks, inspection and inference remain distinct. Skipped checks, unavailable environments and stale pairings prevent unsupported readiness claims.

### Project Configuration

- **Projects can carry their own variants.**
  `variants/<project>/VARIANT.md` owns project identity, planning settings, document homes and mode-specific configuration, with concrete invocations in its adjacent command reference. Selection uses an explicit choice or a unique repository match; unconfigured projects derive settings from their own sources.
- **Workflow-server is a supplied variant.**
  It covers engine and schema checks on `main`, definitions and walks on `workflows`, packaging on `docker`, and scripts, hooks and skills on `workspace`. The common procedures and dependencies remain general.
- **Planning is shared across modes.**
  A shared guide resolves the planning location and reuses the work's record. The selected project supplies its root and naming convention; the mode does not impose a review-specific folder name.

### Skill Maintenance

- **Revise follows the existing skill conventions.**
  Revisions use a worktree, authoritative rule homes, link and structure checks, representative walkthroughs and commit/push delivery.
- **Authoring rules preserve the skill's structure.**
  Rules precede Dependencies, core guidance names individual projects only as examples, and project configuration and shared planning each have one home.
- **Shared guidelines govern selective reading.**
  Authors state applicability beside conditional links, preserve each link's boundary when batching reads, name prerequisites and keep required output complete. Work Designer keeps its representative mode and variant scenarios locally and links to the shared rules.
- **Verification observes delivered instructions.**
  Reading-path changes require realistic requests in independent fresh contexts, repeated scenarios and inspection of actual tool calls, returned content and task results. Necessary consumer guidance can cross modes. Structural checks and live behavior are reported separately; context-token savings require a comparable baseline.

## Test Plan

| Test | Description | Coverage | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | Existing work-planner mode-summary suite: 3 tests pass, including discovery of work-designer | | ✓ |
| T2 | Skill-creator validator accepts the entry point and frontmatter | | ✓ |
| T3 | The 11 skill Markdown files and shared guidelines checked for structure, links and anchors; all 98 local links resolve | | ✓ |
| T4 | All 33 repository source links resolve against the captured local refs; this revision does not change them | | ✓ |
| T5 | Manual walkthroughs cover variant selection, branch-specific Review, Revise consumer guidance, section boundaries, required whole files, prerequisites and missing evidence | | ✓ |
| T6 | Staged diff passes whitespace validation | | ✓ |
| T7 | Two fresh-context Docker Review-planning runs at 0a6ac0b1 use bounded project configuration; one loads the complete variants guide, and both include unneeded conditional command sections | | Partial |
| T8 | Two fresh-context Revise runs on the guideline revision both make the exact isolated template edit and preserve the four baseline files. One uses targeted reads and runs the configured tests; the other loads the whole command catalog and omits the configured summary suite | | Partial |

**Disclosure result: partial pass.** The guideline revision is `453cc4d437686d18370c7cdc66422a442fb5a099`; its four-file contents match the recorded SHA-256 snapshot used by the new Revise evaluations. Both runs read the required authoring guidelines and produced the correct template edit. One selected only relevant command and variant sections; the other reported its unnecessary whole-catalog read and did not resolve the project configuration. No output truncation was observed in these two runs. The parent independently ran the three summary tests on the production revision.

The live evaluations supplied realistic requests and authority limits without expected reading choices or earlier findings. Actual tool calls and returned content were audited. The earlier Review findings remain relevant because its retrieval procedure is not changed here: one run loaded 402 words where the selected section contained 185, and both loaded unneeded shell-syntax and restart command specs.

These cases cover review planning and a small skill revision. They do not establish a completed integration review, consistent minimal reads, or measured context-token savings. The skill as a whole has not met its strict disclosure completion criterion. Evaluation-only template edits remain in isolated worktrees. Local evidence is recorded under `.engineering/artifacts/planning/2026-10-10-1295-work-designer-live-disclosure/`, including `guideline-iteration.md` and the initial `report.md`. Validation retries with authorized host permissions resolved sandbox namespace failures.
